title: The Late Member

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending, and the share circle's envelope sits under the counter at Saduek Sak 24 like a held breath. Mae Tim has walked to the wat to light one candle and not say why.
She sets the change-machine key on the offering ledge beside the candle, then picks it up again. 'A woman running at five percent,' she says, to no one, to the flame.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She turns the change-machine key over in her palm, thumb rubbing the worn brass, and nods at the mattress ad printout under Lek's arm.
turns.dialogue: The vendor's husband is the jealous kind — he counts her phone, not her money. She asks me for two weeks and I hear his voice in it.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She holds up the QR sign from the laundromat wall, its corner curling, and taps the printed code with one fingernail.
turns.dialogue: You read the books for three vendors. What do you think about a circle that lets one wheel go two weeks flat?

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She lifts the phone mount from her bag and sets it on the ledge, screen dark, then turns it face-down.
turns.dialogue: Her daughter just had her heart broken and came home to the cart. That is the two weeks. Not the money — the girl on the mat.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She presses the orange queue vest into Lek's hands and folds his fingers over the fabric, glancing toward the wat door.
turns.dialogue: Don't tell the bench. If the soi hears one member asked, the whole circle starts counting who might ask next.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She unclips the charger bank from the laundromat bench and weighs it in her hand, cord dangling.
turns.dialogue: You're back late from the shop. Good — the bench is empty and I can say this once: I emptied the repair reserve to cover her. The machines are running on nothing now.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She sets the change-machine key down on the biscuit tin lid and pushes both toward Lek across the ledge.
turns.dialogue: We have to do something before Sunday. Either I take her name off the list, or I find the money in the tin. There is no third wheel.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She loops the phone mount back onto her bag strap and steps toward the wat gate, candle still burning behind her.
turns.dialogue: I'm heading out now — the vendor is waiting at the cart. Walk with me or don't, but decide before the soi wakes up.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She stops at the gate and looks at Lek's shoulders, then at the score report sticking out of his bag.
turns.dialogue: Aren't you tired? You carry that paper everywhere like it still weighs something. I have been carrying mine for thirty years and it never got lighter.

mae_turn_1.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_1.line: She names the vendor's husband once, flatly, then puts the key in her pocket. The mattress ad in Lek's hand is for the vendor's daughter's new room — the reason for the two weeks.

mae_turn_2.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_2.line: She waits. The QR sign curls in her fingers, and for once she does not fill the silence with the circle's rules.

mae_turn_3.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_3.line: She turns the phone mount face-down and leaves it there. 'The girl sleeps on the cart mat now. The two weeks are for a mattress, not a debt.'
mae_turn_3.bubble: Mae Tim has named the real reason

mae_turn_4.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_4.line: She takes the vest back and folds it small. 'Then it stays between the two of us and the tin.'

mae_turn_5.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_5.line: She opens the tin and shows him the gap where the repair money was. The ledgers sit lower than they should. 'Sunday the machines stop if one belt goes.'

mae_turn_6.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_6.line: She puts the key on the tin and steps back. 'You keep the vendors' books. Tell me which wheel I can afford to let go flat.'

mae_turn_7.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_7.line: She waits at the gate with the candle behind her, bag on her shoulder, not looking back.

mae_turn_8.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_8.line: She takes the score report out of his bag without asking, reads the three points short, and hands it back. 'We are the same paper, you and me. Only mine got laminated later.'
mae_turn_8.bubble: Mae Tim has seen the score report

finale.dialogue: She blows out the candle and puts the change-machine key back in her pocket. 'Sunday the circle pays her, and I find a belt somewhere. A woman at five percent still walks.'
The wat gate closes behind them. The envelope under the counter is lighter by one name, and the soi does not know it yet.

obj_score_report.name: the laminated score report
obj_score_report.description: Exam result folded twice and laminated at the shop, three points short in red, the lamination bubbled at one corner from a hot iron.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two small keys on a wire ring, one for the stamp drawer and one for the ledger cupboard, worn smooth by nine years of the registrar's thumb.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: Biscuit tin with a picture of a lighthouse, lid dented, holding three vendors' books and a rubber band around the repair envelope.

obj_mattress_ad.name: the mattress ad printout
obj_mattress_ad.description: One-page printout from the copy shop, a mattress on sale, the price circled twice in blue pen.

obj_qr_sign.name: the QR sign
obj_qr_sign.description: Laminated QR code for the laundromat, corner curled from steam, taped at eye level above the change machine.

obj_charger_bank.name: the charger bank
obj_charger_bank.description: Six-port charger bank clamped to the bench, one port dead, cords labeled with masking tape in three hands.

obj_change_key.name: the change-machine key
obj_change_key.description: Brass key on a shoelace, teeth worn round, opens the coin box under the change machine.

obj_phone_mount.name: the phone mount
obj_phone_mount.description: Plastic phone mount for a handlebar, clamp cracked and mended with fishing line, screen-side scratched.

obj_vest_orange.name: the orange queue vest
obj_vest_orange.description: Orange safety vest with a queue number stenciled on the back, reflective strip peeling at the shoulder.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_mae_tim
outcomeRules.line: She reads the three points short and does not hand it back at once. 'You know what it is to be almost. So do I. Show me the tin.'

outcomeRules.speaker: char_mae_tim
outcomeRules.line: She takes the keys, opens the stamp drawer, and counts out the circle's payout in stamps and small notes. 'Sunday she gets paid. The belt can wait one more week.'
outcomeRules.bubble: The circle pays the late member

char_mae_tim: She turns the {item} over once and sets it back on the ledge. 'Not that. Not tonight.'
She looks at the {item}, then at the empty repair envelope in the tin. 'The bench is quiet now. Say what you came to say with the right paper.'
She taps the tin lid. 'The score report first — the one you carry everywhere. Then we talk about the keys.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the bag with nothing settled. The candle burns down; the soi sleeps.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Mae Tim watches the wat door the way she watches the machines spin.
Mae Tim's eyes move from the {item} to the tin and back — a route mapped, a toll implied.
